To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the slow wilting soybean genotype N7001 responds earlier and more efficiently to drought stress than the drought sensitive genotype TJS2049, that this response is mediated by the regulation of specific genes that are differentially expressed between these genotypes, and that one of these genes encodes a eukaryote translation initiation factor, GmeIFisoG-1a, that is involved in the control of general abiotic stress responses in Arabidopsis.

a eukarytic translation initiation factor iso 4G identified by a subtractive hybridization screen of a slow wilting soybean cultivar enhances abiotic stress tolerance in Arabidopsis, and this protein is one of four isoforms in this family in soybean.

the early transcriptional response of a slow wilting soybean genotype to dehydration involves a number of genes encoding regulatory and signaling proteins and that one of these genes, GmeIFisoG-1, confers increased tolerance to abiotic stress when overexpressed in Arabidopsis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying drought tolerance in soybean, and the identification and functional characterization of a gene encoding a eukaryote translation initiation factor, which can be a potential candidate gene for genetic improvement of this important crop.
the identification of molecular mechanisms underlying drought tolerance in soybean.
a better understanding of the molecular and physiological basis of the drought resistance of soybean cultivars and the identification of novel targets for genetic improvement of this crop.

the slow-wilting N7001 cultivar responds to drought by a more efficient water utilization and a more rapid and intense transcriptional reprogramming than the sensitive TJS2041 cultivar.
N7001 has a higher tolerance to drought stress, and this is due to the earlier activation of a larger number of drought responsive genes.
the slow wilting soybean cultivar N7001 responds more efficiently to drought than the sensitive TJS2041 cultivar by up-regulating an earlier and larger number of genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the soybean cultivar N7001, which is characterized as slow wilting, responds to drought by a more efficient water usage than the sensitive cultivar TJS2049, and that this is associated with a more rapid and extensive transcriptional response to drought stress.

we have identified a novel drought-induced protein, a eukaryote translation initiation factor isoform 4G, which when over-expressed in Arabidopsis, enhances tolerance to a variety of abiotic stresses.
we have identified a gene that is up-regulated in a drought tolerant soybean cultivar and that this gene can be used as a marker to select soybean genotypes with increased drought tolerance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we identified a new eIFiso4G isoform that can confer tolerance to multiple abiotic stress in plants.

a eukarytic translation initiation factor (eIFiso4G), which was identified as a dehydration-induced gene in a drought resistant soybean cultivar, when overexpressed in Arabidopsis, conferred the transgenic lines with increased tolerance to a wide range of abiotic stress conditions.
the soybean eukaryotic initiation factor iso4Gs are involved in stress adaptation and that their differential expression is a mechanism to modulate stress tolerance in soybean.
